transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, I came in because I'm having a lot of trouble focusing on my work. I'm a high school teacher, and... I can sit down with a stack of essays to grade, or a curriculum document, fully intending to get to work. But within ten minutes or so, I'll realize I've just been staring at the exact same page. 

I end up thinking about three other things and barely taking in what's actually right in front of me. It's just becoming a real problem, and I need to figure out what's going on.
When did you first start noticing these concentration problems? Have you always had some difficulty focusing, or is this something new that's developed recently?

Well, it's definitely not a new thing. I think it's always been there, honestly. 

Even back in primary school, my report cards used to say things like, uh, "bright but careless," or that I didn't finish my work unless I was closely supervised. And I remember my parents were always finding old worksheets just crumpled up at the bottom of my backpack that I had completely forgotten to turn in. So, yeah, I've had difficulty with this for as long as I can remember.
Besides having trouble focusing, do you find yourself feeling restless or fidgety, or do you tend to act without thinking things through?

No, not really. I wouldn't say I'm restless or fidgety at all. I can sit still at my desk just fine—my problem is more that my mind just wanders off while I'm sitting there. 

And as for acting without thinking... no, I don't think I do that either. If anything, I'm usually pretty careful about things. It's really just the focus and the attention part that I struggle with.

As a child, did you ever have problems with impulsivity—like interrupting people, blurting things out, or having difficulty waiting your turn—or did teachers or parents ever describe you as hyperactive or overly energetic?

No, not really. I wasn't a hyper kid at all. I didn't interrupt or have trouble waiting in line, or anything like that. Honestly, I was actually pretty quiet. 

Teachers never complained about me being disruptive or bouncing off the walls... they just complained that I was daydreaming or not finishing my assignments. So, no, I didn't have those kinds of issues with being overly energetic.
Beyond your work as a teacher, have these attention and focus problems affected other areas of your life—like your relationships, managing household tasks, or other responsibilities?

Yeah, it definitely spills over into other parts of my life. 

At work, the issue with not following through on things has gotten pretty serious. My department chair actually put me on a support plan recently because I was missing too many deadlines and forgetting administrative tasks. 

And at home... well, it affects my marriage, too. My wife has basically had to take over paying all the bills and keeping track of reminders for things we need to do. She just feels like she can't count on me to stay on top of them, and honestly, she's right. So, yeah, it's definitely causing problems outside of just the classroom.
Looking back to when you were around 5 to 12 years old, would you say these attention problems were present and noticeable during that time period?

Yeah, they definitely were. Even back in primary school, my report cards always had comments like, uh, "bright but careless," or that I wouldn't finish my work unless I was being closely supervised. And my parents were constantly finding old worksheets just crumpled up at the bottom of my backpack—assignments I had completely forgotten to turn in. So, yeah, it's been going on since I was pretty young.
Have you ever been diagnosed with depression, anxiety, or any other mental health condition? And if so, when did that start relative to when you first noticed these attention problems?
No, I haven't. I've never been diagnosed with depression or anxiety, or anything else like that. It's really just been this ongoing struggle with focus and getting things done.

Do you find yourself struggling to organize your tasks and materials—like having trouble keeping track of where you put things, or difficulty planning out how to tackle a big project? Or do you frequently forget things you're supposed to do, even important ones?

Yeah, I definitely forget things I'm supposed to do. Probably more than I want to admit, honestly. It's just ordinary responsibilities that slip my mind. Like, I'll completely forget to reply to an email from a student's parent, or I'll forget to pay a bill until we get a late notice in the mail. Or my wife will ask me to pick something up from the store on my way home from school, and I'll just walk in the front door empty-handed because it completely left my head. It happens a lot.
When you sit down to grade those essays or plan out a lesson, do you find it hard to organize your approach—like, do you struggle to figure out where to start or how to break the task into steps?

Actually, no, I don't really have a problem with that part. When I sit down to plan a lesson or grade a stack of essays, I usually know exactly what steps to take and where to start. Breaking the task down makes sense to me. So, no, the actual organizing of how to approach the work isn't really an issue for me.

You mentioned you're not restless or fidgety at your desk, but I want to ask more specifically: do you find yourself frequently tapping your fingers or feet, shifting around in your seat, or having an urge to move around even when you're trying to stay focused on something?

No, not really. I don't really tap my feet or fidget with my hands. I mean, I might shift in my chair sometimes like anyone else getting comfortable, but I don't have this urge to get up and move around or anything like that. I can sit still just fine.
Looking back at your childhood, would you say these attention and focus problems were noticeable and causing you difficulty before you turned 12 years old?

Yes, definitely. Even back in primary school, it was an issue. I remember my report cards always had comments like, "bright but careless," or they'd say I wouldn't finish my work unless the teacher was standing right there watching me. And my parents were constantly finding crumpled up worksheets at the bottom of my backpack that I had completely forgotten to turn in. So, yeah, it's been happening since I was a kid.
